title: E2E: validate attachment flow end to end
description:
Run all quality gates and produce a manual test plan for the attachment flow.

**What:** Final validation — cargo test, clippy, fmt; plus manual test checklist.

**Algorithm:**
1. Run `cargo fmt --all` — commit any format changes.
2. Run `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings` — must exit 0.
3. Run `cargo test --workspace` — must exit 0, all tests pass.
4. Verify web/app.js exports: formatBytes, uploadBlob, buildAttachmentElement, callJmap, bootstrap, showError, hideError, getContactName, fetchContacts, renderContactList, openOrCreateChat, fetchChats, getChatDisplayName, renderChatList, selectChat, fetchMessages, getSenderLabel, createMessageBubble, renderThread, appendMessageBubble, setupCompose, startEventSource — all must be present.
5. Verify no innerHTML for attachment data (grep web/app.js for innerHTML — any hits involving attachment field must be flagged as a bug).

**Manual test plan (record as bd note):**
- Step 1: Start kithd with --data-dir and --cert.
- Step 2: Open web client in browser. Verify attach button (📎) appears next to Send.
- Step 3: Click 📎, select a small file (< 1 MB). Verify: preview shows filename + size below textarea; no error.
- Step 4: Type a message body, click Send. Verify: message appears in thread with attachment filename as download link and size.
- Step 5: Click the download link. Verify: browser downloads the file with correct name.
- Step 6: From a second kithd instance (peer), send a message with attachment. Verify: received message shows attachment link in web client.
- Step 7: Attempt to attach a 101 MB file. Verify: error banner shows 'File too large'.
- Step 8: Send a message with no attachment. Verify: no attachments field in bubble, no regression.

**Defensive rules:**
- cargo test must pass without modification to any test (test integrity rule).
- If any cargo command fails, do not close this bead — report the failure.
notes: Manual test plan: (1) start kithd; (2) open web client; verify 📎 button next to Send; (3) click 📎, select file < 1MB; verify preview shows filename+size; (4) type body, Send; verify message thread shows attachment link; (5) click link, verify download; (6) try 101MB file, verify 'File too large' error; (7) send message with no file, verify no regression.
